sentences.en: Seattle is a city with plenty of well-known tourist attractions.
sentences.zh: 西雅图是一座拥有众多知名旅游景点的城市。

sentences.en: The Space Needle, Pike Place Market, the Seattle Art Museum.
sentences.zh: 太空针塔、派克市场、西雅图艺术博物馆。

sentences.en: Today, though, I'm venturing out in the rain to visit a different sort of Seattle attraction.
sentences.zh: 不过今天，我要冒着雨去参观一种不同类型的西雅图景点。

sentences.en: It's an office building called the Bullet Center.
sentences.zh: 那是一栋名为“布利特中心”的办公大楼。

sentences.en: I'm here to meet Brian Court, one of the architects.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是为了见布赖恩·库尔特，他是建筑师之一。

sentences.en: Thank you for doing this at short notice.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你在百忙之中抽出时间。

sentences.en: Brian and I are headed to the top floor.
sentences.zh: 我和布赖恩正前往顶楼。

sentences.en: My first instinct is to find the elevator, but it's nowhere in sight.
sentences.zh: 我的第一直觉是找电梯，但它却不见踪影。

sentences.en: Did you forget to put an elevator in the building, Brian?
sentences.zh: 布赖恩，你是不是忘了在楼里装电梯了？

sentences.en: We do have an elevator through the door to the left.
sentences.zh: 我们左手边的门里确实有一部电梯。

sentences.en: If you're in a wheelchair or you're not able to climb the stairs,
sentences.zh: 如果你坐轮椅或者无法爬楼梯，

sentences.en: you just hit the button there with the wheelchair and that door will open.
sentences.zh: 你只需按一下那里的轮椅按钮，门就会打开。

sentences.en: But we were trying to give people an option to take the stair firSt.
sentences.zh: 但我们试图为人们提供一个首先选择走楼梯的选项。

sentences.en: There are six floors of Douglas First Steps built on an outer wall of the building.
sentences.zh: 大楼的外墙上建有六层楼高的道格拉斯步道。

sentences.en: Each floor has expansive landings that allow people to congregate and chat.
sentences.zh: 每层楼都有宽敞的平台，供人们聚集和聊天。

sentences.en: The best views at the Bullet Center are not from the CEO's office.
sentences.zh: 在布利特中心，最好的风景并非来自首席执行官的办公室。

sentences.en: You get those views when you climb what people here refer to as the irresistible staircase.
sentences.zh: 当你攀登被这里的人们称为“无法抗拒的楼梯”时，你就能欣赏到这些风景。

sentences.en: So you walk into the stair enclosure, you look up, you see the stair all the way up to the sixth floor of the building,
sentences.zh: 所以你走进楼梯间，抬头看，能看到一直通往大楼六楼的楼梯，

sentences.en: and that's hopefully going to draw you up the stair.
sentences.zh: 希望这能吸引你走上楼梯。

sentences.en: The designers wanted to build a staircase that would help people become healthier.
sentences.zh: 设计者希望建造一个能帮助人们变得更健康的楼梯。

sentences.en: Their intuition was that if the stairs were appealing and prominent, people would use them.
sentences.zh: 他们的直觉是，如果楼梯既吸引人又显眼，人们就会使用它们。

sentences.en: What you see as you climb to the sixth floor are sweeping views of Seattle.
sentences.zh: 当你爬到六楼时，映入眼帘的是西雅图的全景。

sentences.en: You'll notice as we get higher, the views of the city really start to unfold.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到，随着我们越爬越高，城市的景色真正开始展开。

sentences.en: This corner of the project site had some of the best views you can see out now to the west
sentences.zh: 项目用地的这个角落拥有你可以看到的最佳视野，现在向西望去，

sentences.en: and then the downtown skyline directly to the south.
sentences.zh: 然后是正南方的市中心天际线。

sentences.en: By putting a stair here, we were able to really capitalize on views all the way from the east around to the weSt.
sentences.zh: 通过在这里建造楼梯，我们能够真正充分利用从东到西的视野。

sentences.en: So far, Brian says, this irresistible staircase seems to be living up to its name.
sentences.zh: 布赖恩说，到目前为止，这个无法抗拒的楼梯似乎名副其实。

sentences.en: We've actually got data that's showing us that just about two-thirds of the people
sentences.zh: 我们实际获得的数据显示，大约三分之二的人

sentences.en: that go to the sixth floor on a daily basis are taking the stair over the elevator.
sentences.zh: 每天去六楼时都选择走楼梯而不是乘电梯。

sentences.en: Most buildings place the elevators front and center as you walk inside.
sentences.zh: 大多数建筑在人们走进去时，都会把电梯放在显眼的正中央。

sentences.en: Most of us don't even think to look for the stairs when we enter an office building.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人在进入办公楼时，甚至都不会想到去寻找楼梯。

sentences.en: By making the stairs prominent and keeping the elevators out of sight,
sentences.zh: 通过让楼梯显眼并将电梯藏在视线之外，

sentences.en: the bullet center is trying to get people to develop new behaviors.
sentences.zh: 布利特中心正试图让人们养成新的行为习惯。

sentences.en: Sometimes, unexpected things happen as you climb these stairs.
sentences.zh: 有时候，当你爬这些楼梯时，会发生意想不到的事情。

sentences.en: You bump into people you didn't think you'd meet.
sentences.zh: 你会偶遇你以为不会遇到的人。

sentences.en: When I was passing, I heard you talk about me walking up the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我路过时，听到你们在谈论我爬楼梯的事。

sentences.en: I was like, that sounded like, is that?
sentences.zh: 我想，听起来好像是，是吗？

sentences.en: So, I just wanted to come down and say hello.
sentences.zh: 所以，我只是想下来打个招呼。

sentences.en: He walked down a flight of stairs to come say hello.
sentences.zh: 他走下一段楼梯来打招呼。

sentences.en: He told me he takes the stairs nearly every day.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他几乎每天都走楼梯。

sentences.en: And he often has chance interactions on them that turn out to be very enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 而且他经常在楼梯上偶遇，结果总是非常愉快。

sentences.en: Do you actually think about it each day, that you're saying, I want to take the stairs,
sentences.zh: 你每天真的会去想这件事吗，比如“我想走楼梯”，

sentences.en: or is it just sort of an unconscious decision at this point?
sentences.zh: 还是说到了这个阶段，这只是一种无意识的决定？

sentences.en: There are some times when I'm coming from downtown and I've walked all the way up Capitol Hill
sentences.zh: 有时我从市中心过来，一路走上国会山，

sentences.en: and I get to the door of the building and I think, oh man, another six flights?
sentences.zh: 当我走到大楼门口时，我想，天哪，又是六层楼？

sentences.en: But then I think, you know, I don't get a whole lot of exercise in my day-to-day work life anyway,
sentences.zh: 但接着我想，你知道的，我的日常工作生活中本来就没有太多锻炼，

sentences.en: and so this is worth it, and I enjoy the view, always.
sentences.zh: 所以这是值得的，而且我总是很享受这里的风景。

sentences.en: There's a word for such behaviors.
This week on Hidden Brain, we consider how habits shape who we are
sentences.zh: 本周的“隐藏的大脑”，我们将探讨习惯如何塑造了我们，

sentences.en: and how we can use them to become the people we'd like to be.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何利用习惯成为我们想要成为的人。

sentences.en: You probably know someone like this in your life.
sentences.zh: 你生活中可能认识这样的人。

sentences.en: The person who gets a ton of things done, eats healthy food, and stays in shape.
sentences.zh: 能完成大量工作、吃健康食品并保持体形的人。

sentences.en: People like Chris Traeger from the TV series Parks and Recreation.
sentences.zh: 比如电视剧《公园与游憩》中的克里斯·特雷格。

sentences.en: I have to go run 10 miles.
I have run 10 miles a day, every day, for 18 years.
A third of the way to the moon.
sentences.zh: 到月球距离的三分之一。

sentences.en: My goal is to run to the moon.
Picture a guy who strips off his work clothes to reveal a running outfit underneath.
sentences.zh: 想象一个脱掉工作服，露出里面跑步装备的家伙。

sentences.en: Now, Chris Traeger is a fictional character, exaggerated for comedic effect.
sentences.zh: 现在，克里斯·特雷格是一个虚构人物，为了喜剧效果而夸张了。

sentences.en: But we all know someone like this, a friend or colleague or spouse,
sentences.zh: 但我们都认识这样的人，一个朋友、同事或配偶，

sentences.en: who consistently performs the tasks that seem so hard to the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 他们始终如一地执行那些对我们其余人来说似乎很难的任务。

sentences.en: What do they have that the rest of us lack?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么是我们其他人所缺乏的？

sentences.en: According to Wendy Wood, a professor of psychology and business at the University of Southern California,
sentences.zh: 根据南加州大学心理学和商业教授温迪·伍德的说法，

sentences.en: characters like Chris Traeger are not magical unicorns.
sentences.zh: 像克里斯·特雷格这样的人物并非神奇的独角兽。
他们只是掌握了一个秘密。

sentences.en: They are expert at building good habits.
sentences.zh: 他们是培养好习惯的专家。

sentences.en: In her book, Good Habits, Bad Habits, The Science of Making Positive Changes That Stick,
sentences.zh: 在她的小说《好习惯，坏习惯：建立持久积极改变的科学》中，

sentences.en: Wendy argues that we can all become experts at building good habits and dismantling bad ones
sentences.zh: 温迪认为，我们都可以成为培养好习惯和打破坏习惯的专家，

sentences.en: if we only stop to understand the psychology behind our routines.
sentences.zh: 只要我们停下来去理解我们日常行为背后的心理学。
温迪，欢迎来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm thrilled to be here.
I want to start with something that you once saw on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我想从你曾在脸书上看到的一件事开始。

sentences.en: Your cousin went on Facebook and announced that she was going to change her life,
sentences.zh: 你的表妹在脸书上宣布她要改变自己的生活，

sentences.en: by which she meant she wanted to lose some weight.
sentences.zh: 意思是她想减掉一些体重。

sentences.en: Why did she announce this on Facebook?
sentences.zh: 她为什么要在这个平台上宣布这一点？

sentences.en: And what was the reaction she garnered from her friends?
sentences.zh: 她从朋友那里得到了什么反应？

sentences.en: So I think by making a public statement,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为通过发表公开声明，

sentences.en: she was trying to commit herself to the initial idea, her initial desire to lose weight.
sentences.zh: 她试图让自己致力于最初的想法，她减肥的最初愿望。

sentences.en: In a way, she sort of upped the stakes because she made it public.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，她提高了赌注，因为她将其公开了。

sentences.en: And then she was accountable to all of her Facebook friends.
sentences.zh: 然后她对她所有的脸书朋友负有责任。
他们给予了极大的支持。

sentences.en: They spurred her on and told her how strong she was.
sentences.zh: 他们鼓励她，告诉她她是多么坚强。

sentences.en: So she got a lot of positive reinforcement for that.
sentences.zh: 所以她为此得到了很多积极的强化。

sentences.en: And the feedback from her friends, this idea of encouraging her, telling her, just do it,
sentences.zh: 来自朋友们的反馈，这种鼓励她、告诉她“放手去做”的想法，

sentences.en: you know, that reminds me of a video made by the actor Shia LaBeouf.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这让我想起了演员希亚·拉博夫制作的一段视频。

sentences.en: He stands in front of a green screen and he says,
actually, let me just play for you what he says.
sentences.zh: 实际上，让我给你们播放一下他说的话。

sentences.en: This message, Wendy, is so pervasive when it comes to making changes in our life.
sentences.zh: 温迪，当谈到在我们生活中做出改变时，这个信息是如此无处不在。

sentences.en: The idea that if you want to make a change, all you have to do is just say, just do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想做出改变，你所需要做的就是说“只管去做”。

sentences.en: I don't think that's most of our experience.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不是我们大多数人的经验。

sentences.en: But what we do believe is if we wanted to enough, we'd exert enough willpower and we'd make it happen.
sentences.zh: 但我们所相信的是，如果我们足够想这么做，我们就会施加足够的意志力，并使其发生。

sentences.en: And the result, though, is that it doesn't often, because willpower is not actually, we have found,
sentences.zh: 然而结果是，这种情况并不常见，因为我们发现意志力实际上并不是

sentences.en: the best way to achieve our goals and to change our behavior.
sentences.zh: 实现我们目标和改变行为的最佳方式。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea, Wendy, that significant numbers of Americans believe that the way to change their behavior is through self-control,
sentences.zh: 温迪，谈谈这个观点，相当一部分美国人认为改变行为的方式是通过自我控制，

sentences.en: that willpower is the key to either making changes that stick or to making changes that fail to stick.
sentences.zh: 意志力是实现持久改变或导致改变无法持久的关键。

sentences.en: It's something that pervades our culture.
sentences.zh: 这是充斥我们文化的一种东西。

sentences.en: When surveys are done of Americans and their beliefs about how to change behavior,
sentences.zh: 当对美国人及其关于如何改变行为的信念进行调查时，
特别是像肥胖这样的问题，

sentences.en: three quarters of Americans think that it's a problem with self-control and willpower,
sentences.zh: 四分之三的美国人认为这是自我控制和意志力的问题，

sentences.en: that we just don't have enough.
sentences.zh: 认为我们拥有的还不够。

sentences.en: And if we had more, we'd all be thinner.
sentences.zh: 如果我们有更多，我们都会变瘦。

sentences.en: Now, researchers have actually looked at this question and asked how much willpower is central.
sentences.zh: 现在，研究人员实际上已经研究了这个问题，并询问意志力有多核心。

sentences.en: You cite the work of the late, great psychologist Daniel Wegner,
sentences.zh: 你引用了已故伟大的心理学家丹尼尔·韦格纳的工作，

sentences.en: who once ran a study where he told people not to think about a white bear.
sentences.zh: 他曾做过一项研究，告诉人们不要去想一只白熊。

sentences.en: He did it to show that if you try not to think about something,
sentences.zh: 他这样做是为了表明，如果你试图不去想某事，

sentences.en: even something as trivial as a white bear that you wouldn't normally think about,
sentences.zh: 甚至像你平时不会想到的白熊这样微不足道的事情，

sentences.en: then later, when you're given an opportunity to think about it again,
sentences.zh: 那么后来，当你再次有机会去想它时，

sentences.en: It's a white bear, white bear, white pear.
So this tells us something about what it's like to try to repress or control our desires.
sentences.zh: 这向我们展示了试图压抑或控制我们的欲望是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Yes, we can do it in the short run, but ultimately, it backfires.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在短期内可以做到，但最终会适得其反。

sentences.en: Those ideas get a life of their own and they start to obsess us.
sentences.zh: 这些想法有了它们自己的生命，并开始让我们着迷。

sentences.en: And when you think about the behaviors we often want to change in our lives,
sentences.zh: 当你想到我们经常想要改变生活中的行为时，

sentences.en: quitting smoking or eating healthier or exercising more regularly,
sentences.zh: 戒烟、吃得更健康或更有规律地锻炼，

sentences.en: the challenge, of course, is not to make a one-time change, not to exercise well just today.
sentences.zh: 当然，挑战不在于进行一次性改变，不在于今天锻炼好就行。

sentences.en: The challenge, of course, is to make a long-term change.
sentences.zh: 当然，挑战在于做出长期改变。

sentences.en: And the research would then suggest that willpower might not be the most effective way to go about
sentences.zh: 研究表明，意志力可能不是实现这一目标的

sentences.en: Yes, that's actually how I got into this whole research area.
sentences.zh: 是的，这实际上是我涉足整个研究领域的契机。

sentences.en: I was interested in understanding what it is that helps people persiSt.
sentences.zh: 我有兴趣了解是什么帮助人们坚持下去。

sentences.en: So how do people persist at, say, eating healthfully or saving more money or getting more sleep?
sentences.zh: 那么人们是如何坚持健康饮食、存更多钱或获得更多睡眠的呢？

sentences.en: We can all do this one time or two times, but it's a very different thing to do it on a consistent basis.
sentences.zh: 我们都可以做一两次，但要持续不断地做到这一点则是完全不同的另一回事。

sentences.en: When I first started this research, the idea was that we did these things when we were sufficiently committed,
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始这项研究时，人们的想法是，当我们有足够的承诺时，我们就会做这些事情，

sentences.en: when we had enough self-control to follow through.
sentences.zh: 当我们有足够的自我控制力去执行时。

sentences.en: Then we'd form these strong intentions and we'd act on them over time.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会形成这些坚定的意图，并随着时间的推移采取行动。

sentences.en: But I'd noticed that it didn't really play out that way in my life.
sentences.zh: 但我注意到，在我的生活中，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: I've often made decisions that I didn't follow through with,
sentences.zh: 我经常做出最终没有兑现的决定，

sentences.en: even though I was initially very committed to those decisions.
sentences.zh: 尽管我最初对这些决定非常坚定。

sentences.en: And I have a pretty good amount of willpower.
sentences.zh: 而且我的意志力其实挺强的。

sentences.en: So what we did is we did a large review of the research
sentences.zh: 所以我们做的是，对相关研究进行了大规模梳理

sentences.en: to test whether people's decision-making was important
sentences.zh: 来检验人们的决策是否重要

sentences.en: all the way through behavior change process,
sentences.zh: 贯穿整个行为改变的过程，

sentences.en: not just from the beginning, where my cousin started on Facebook declaring she's going to change,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是从一开始——比如我表姐在脸书上宣布她要改变时，

sentences.en: but also two, three months later.
And what we found was really surprising.
sentences.zh: 而我们的发现着实令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Decision-making, our intentions, our thoughts, our commitment,
sentences.zh: 决策、我们的意图、我们的想法、我们的决心，

sentences.en: they're very important when we start to change.
sentences.zh: 在刚开始改变时它们非常重要。

sentences.en: That's what determines whether we do behaviors once in a while.
sentences.zh: 这决定了我们是否会偶尔做出某种行为。

sentences.en: Well, continuing over time took something very different.
sentences.zh: 然而，要长久地坚持下去，则需要完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: And we didn't know what it was to start off with.
sentences.zh: 一开始我们并不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: It was like once you start performing a behavior,
sentences.zh: 这就好比一旦你开始执行某种行为，

sentences.en: it just sort of continues on its own.
sentences.zh: 它就会顺理成章地继续下去。

sentences.en: And what we decided was this is kind of like driving your car, right?
sentences.zh: 我们得出的结论是，这有点像开车，对吧？

sentences.en: So every once in a while you do pay attention and make decisions,
sentences.zh: 所以你偶尔确实会集中注意力并做决策，

sentences.en: but most of the time when you're driving, it's sort of in the background.
sentences.zh: 但当你开车时，大部分时间它都处于后台运行状态。

sentences.en: You're thinking about something other than what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你脑子里想的往往不是你正在做的事。

sentences.en: Your actual responses don't take much thought and decision.
sentences.zh: 你的实际反应并不需要太多的思考和决策。

sentences.en: They're certainly not taking your willpower.
sentences.zh: 它们当然也用不上你的意志力。
这是一个违反直觉的想法。

sentences.en: Conscious willpower is not the driving force behind sustained behavior change.
sentences.zh: 有意识的意志力并不是持续改变行为的驱动力。

sentences.en: That idea is powerfully illustrated by an experiment conducted in Germany
sentences.zh: 德国开展的一项实验强有力地证明了这一点，
该实验提出了两个简单的问题。

sentences.en: Are people who stick to their resolutions the people who see lots of temptations
sentences.zh: 那些坚持目标的人，是因为他们面临很多诱惑

sentences.en: but have the willpower to resist them?
sentences.zh: 但有意志力去抗拒它们吗？

sentences.en: Or are they the kind of people who've set up their lives
sentences.zh: 还是说，他们是那种将生活安排妥当，

sentences.en: so they don't even notice the temptations?
sentences.zh: 以至于根本注意不到诱惑的人？

sentences.en: They found that contrary to all of our expectations,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，与我们所有人的预期相反，
